lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` root route returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open the URL in your browser.

targets.caption: Decorator registering the root GET path
Click this URL to open your API

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
The @app.get decorator defines a path for HTTP GET
The "/" path is the root route
uvicorn main:app means file name and app variable name
--reload restarts the server when the file changes

hints: Install both packages first: pip install fastapi uvicorn.
In main.py, import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), then decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the folder that contains main.py, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser.
If uvicorn reports it can't import the module, check that the file is named main.py and the variable is named app (or adjust main:app to match).
common_mistakes: Installing fastapi but forgetting uvicorn, so the uvicorn command is not found.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, causing 'Could not import module "main"'.
Typing uvicorn main.py or main:App instead of main:app (the module name has no .py and the variable name must match).
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI(), which assigns the class instead of an app instance.
Putting the decorator on a line not directly above the function, or forgetting to return the dictionary.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add an empty `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. Test with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Empty list that holds the items

explanations.topic: What routes are in FastAPI
Using a list as in-memory storage for to-do items
POST request to the /items path
Function argument becomes a query parameter
Returning the whole list to see results
Passing the item via ?item= in curl

hints: Define the list `items = []` at module level, outside any function, so it persists between requests.
Use the `@app.post("/items")` decorator above a function named `create_item` that takes `item: str`.
Inside the function, call `items.append(item)` and then `return items`.
Keep uvicorn running in one terminal and run `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'` in a second terminal. Quote the URL so the shell doesn't mangle the `?`.
common_mistakes: Defining `items = []` inside the function, so the list resets on every request and only ever holds one item.
Using `@app.get` instead of `@app.post`, so the curl POST returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Forgetting `-X POST` in curl, which sends a GET and returns 405.
Leaving the URL unquoted in the shell, so `?` is treated as a glob and fails or gets mangled.
Omitting `?item=...`, which returns a 422 error saying the field is required.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running it with --reload), so the new route returns 404 Not Found.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint for one item
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add items, then curl `/items/0` and `/items/1`.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with a path parameter
Fetch the first item by index

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly braces map to function arguments
Auto-reload resets the in-memory items list
Path value becomes the function variable
Type hints make FastAPI convert the path value

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator as before, but put a variable name in curly braces inside the path.
The variable name in the braces must match a parameter of your function, e.g. item_id.
Annotate the parameter as int so you can use it as a list index, then return items[item_id].
The server reloaded and emptied the list: POST a couple of items again before curling /items/0.
common_mistakes: Testing right after saving without re-adding items, so items[0] raises IndexError (500 Internal Server Error).
Leaving out the int type hint, so item_id arrives as a string and indexing the list fails.
Function parameter name not matching the {item_id} placeholder in the path.
Forgetting the curly braces and writing the literal path /items/item_id.
Requesting an index beyond the list length (e.g. /items/3), which gives a 500 error until 404 handling is added in the next step.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import `HTTPException` from fastapi and in get_item raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...)` when the index is out of range. Curl a missing index to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Raise a 404 with a helpful detail

explanations.topic: Why an internal server error isn't helpful for a missing item
HTTP status codes: client errors and 404 Not Found
HTTPException status_code and detail parameters

hints: Missing items should give the client a 404 Not Found instead of a 500 error. FastAPI provides an exception class you can raise for this.
Add HTTPException to your `from fastapi import ...` line.
In get_item, check `if item_id < len(items):` and return the item. Otherwise raise the exception.
Use `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`, then curl an index past the end of the list.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`. The exception object gets returned and the client doesn't receive a 404.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError (500) when a missing item is requested.
Using `<=` instead of `<` in the length check. Requesting index len(items) then still causes an IndexError.
Testing with an index that exists, so the 404 response never appears.
Running uvicorn without --reload and not restarting it, so the old handler still returns an Internal Server Error.

steps.title: List items with limit query parameter
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Curl `/items?limit=3` and `/items` to compare.

explanations.topic: Path vs query parameters in FastAPI
FastAPI converts query strings to the annotated type (int)
limit slices the list; default value comes from the function signature
Same /items path, different HTTP method routes to a different function

hints: Add a new route for GET requests on "/items", the same path your POST endpoint uses.
Give the function a parameter limit annotated as int with a default of 10. FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return a slice of your list: items[0:limit].
Add several items with POST first, then curl '/items?limit=3' and '/items' and compare how many come back.
common_mistakes: Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the request hits the create endpoint.
Forgetting the int annotation, so limit stays a string and slicing raises a TypeError.
Testing with an empty list after restarting uvicorn. The in-memory items are lost, so both requests return [].
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so ? or & gets interpreted by the shell.
Putting limit in the path as /items/{limit} instead of using it as a query parameter.

steps.title: Use a Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: Import `BaseModel` from pydantic, define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and use `item: Item` in create_item. POST JSON with curl and verify a missing text field fails validation.

explanations.topic: Pydantic models give structure and validation
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not query params
Default value is_done=False filled in
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Start with `from pydantic import BaseModel`, then subclass it as `class Item(BaseModel):`.
Give Item two fields: `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and change create_item's parameter to `item: Item`.
The old `?item=apple` query string no longer works: send JSON with `-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}'` and drop the query parameter.
To test validation, send `-d '{"title":"apple"}'`. The response should be a 422 error saying `text` is missing.
common_mistakes: Leaving `?item=apple` on the URL instead of sending a JSON body, which gives a 422 error.
Forgetting the `Content-Type: application/json` header in curl.
Writing `class Item:` without inheriting from BaseModel.
Giving `text` a default value, so a missing text field does not fail validation.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running with --reload), so the old string-based endpoint still runs.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: Add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Reload and confirm responses still work.

explanations.topic: Modeling responses with the same Pydantic BaseModel
response_model argument on the route decorator
Response model for a list of items
Why response models help clients conform to the API

hints: The response model goes in the route decorator, not in the function body.
Add a keyword argument to @app.get(...) for get_item: response_model=Item.
For the list endpoint, wrap the model in a list type: response_model=list[Item].
Save the file; with --reload uvicorn restarts. Hit /items and /items/0 to confirm they still return JSON.
common_mistakes: Using response_model=[Item] or response_model=Item on the list route instead of list[Item].
Spelling it responseModel or response_models — FastAPI rejects unknown kwargs.
Putting response_model on the POST create route only and leaving the GET routes unchanged.
Using list[Item] on Python < 3.9 without importing List from typing, causing a TypeError at startup.
Returning a dict missing a required Item field, which now triggers a ResponseValidationError (500).

steps.title: Explore the interactive docs
steps.instructions: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, use Try it out on POST /items and Execute a request. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click Try it out on POST /items
Send the request from Swagger UI

explanations.topic: FastAPI auto-generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Execute shows the equivalent curl command and sends a real request
/redoc is an alternative documentation view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses for client generation

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in the browser.
Expand the POST /items endpoint, click 'Try it out', edit the request body JSON, then click 'Execute'.
Scroll down below Execute to see the curl command and the Response body.
Change the path to /redoc for the alternate docs, and click the small /openapi.json link under the page title to see the raw schema.
common_mistakes: Opening /docs while the uvicorn server is stopped, so the page fails to load.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out', so the request body can't be edited.
Sending a request body that doesn't match the Item model, which returns a 422 validation error.
Typing /doc or /docs/ with a typo instead of /docs.
Editing the body with invalid JSON, such as trailing commas or single quotes.
